portrait.wry: Augustin, the Concierge, with a wry look

firstCascade.0: Your first cascade. Welcome; I am Augustin, at your service.
firstCascade.1: A cascade already. Augustin, Concierge. Do carry on exactly like that.
firstCascade.2: Splendid start. I am Augustin; whatever you need, I have arranged it.
firstCascade.3: There it is, your first cascade. The house is delighted to meet you.
firstCascade.4: Welcome aboard. Augustin, Concierge. I had a feeling about you.

chic.0: {{coins}} coins in a row. Chic, and quite right.
chic.1: Chic. Understated, tasteful, {{coins}} coins. I approve.
chic.2: A chic little cascade. One does like a tidy {{coins}}.
chic.3: {{coins}} coins tumbling in good order. Very chic.
chic.4: Chic. The sort of thing one mentions casually at dinner.

lavish.0: Lavish. {{coins}} coins, and not a hair out of place.
lavish.1: Now that is lavish. I shall have the brass polished in your honour.
lavish.2: {{coins}} coins. Lavish. The staff are pretending not to stare.
lavish.3: A lavish cascade. You do spoil the table.
lavish.4: Lavish, if I may say so. And I may; I am the Concierge.

opulent.0: Opulent. {{coins}} coins; the chandeliers are trembling with envy.
opulent.1: {{coins}} coins! Opulent. I may need to sit down, discreetly.
opulent.2: Opulent. I have seen dukes do less with more.
opulent.3: An opulent cascade. Shall I ring for more champagne?
opulent.4: Opulent, truly. The yacht sits a little lower in the water.

decadent.0: Decadent. {{coins}} coins. I shan’t tell anyone. Much.
decadent.1: {{coins}} coins? Decadent. Mother would not approve. I rather do.
decadent.2: Decadent. One more and I shall fetch the smelling salts.
decadent.3: A decadent cascade. How terribly, wonderfully excessive.
decadent.4: Decadent. I am obliged to frown. I am failing.

obscene.0: OBSCENE! Cover the ladies’ eyes. And the gentlemen’s.
obscene.1: Good heavens. That was OBSCENE. Do it again.
obscene.2: OBSCENE! The other guests are fanning themselves.
obscene.3: My monocle! That was, there is no other word, OBSCENE.
obscene.4: OBSCENE. I shall write to the papers about this. Fondly.

first.0: Three alike, and now {{tier}}. Your first fusion.
first.1: Your first fusion, and {{tier}} for your trouble. Keep them close.
first.2: Three alike make one finer: {{tier}}. Now you know the house secret.
first.3: A fusion! {{tier}}, born of good company. Well spotted.
first.4: First fusion: {{tier}}. Keep matching coins together; they get ideas.

minor.1: Another fusion: {{tier}}. Your coins have excellent manners.
minor.4: {{tier}}, freshly struck. I do like to see coins get along.

platinum.1: A platinum coin. I shall have it announced at dinner.
platinum.2: Platinum! The house silver feels quite inadequate.
platinum.3: Platinum, in the flesh. Or rather, in the metal.
platinum.4: Platinum. You are moving up in the world, and the world has noticed.

diamond.0: A diamond coin. I may need a moment.
diamond.1: Diamond! Mind the glare; it is terribly bright.
diamond.2: Diamond. The jewellers of Monaco will be furious.
diamond.3: A diamond coin. Even I am impressed, and I have carried a sultan’s luggage.
diamond.4: Diamond. I shall bring out the good velvet.

heirloom.0: An HEIRLOOM? On my table? I must sit down.
heirloom.1: Heirloom! Generations will squabble over that one.
heirloom.2: Good heavens, an heirloom coin. I had only read about those.
heirloom.3: An heirloom. My monocle has quite fallen out.
heirloom.4: HEIRLOOM. Call the family solicitor. Call everyone.

perfect.0: A perfect pour. Not a drop wasted.
perfect.1: Perfect. The sommelier is weeping with pride.
perfect.2: On the beat, every coin. Exquisite timing.
perfect.3: A perfect pour. You have done this before, I think.
perfect.4: Perfect. I could not have poured it better myself, and I have tried.

warning.0: Gently, please. The cabinet is antique.
warning.1: One more shove and I shall have to ring the bell.
warning.2: Decorum, I beg you. The other guests are looking.
warning.3: We nudge; we do not wrestle. A little restraint.
warning.4: Ahem. The table is not a dance partner.

freeze.0: That will do! The table rests for {{seconds}} seconds.
freeze.1: Really! {{seconds}} seconds of quiet reflection, if you please.
freeze.2: Ding! Hands off the cabinet for {{seconds}} seconds.
freeze.3: Scandalous! I am closing the table for {{seconds}} seconds.
freeze.4: Enough. Compose yourself; the table reopens in {{seconds}} seconds.

stillFrozen.0: Patience. The table is still collecting itself.
stillFrozen.1: Not yet. I did say a few seconds, and I meant it.
stillFrozen.2: Still resting. Perhaps admire the view meanwhile?
stillFrozen.3: The table is sulking. Give it a moment.
stillFrozen.4: Soon. Good things come to those who stop shoving.

aimCentre.0: If I may: the side gutters keep everything. Aim for the middle of the table.
aimCentre.1: Coins dropped near the centre fall off the front, which is where they pay.
aimCentre.2: The sides are rather greedy tonight. Try dropping closer to the middle.
aimCentre.3: Those edges swallow coins whole. Centre your drops; the front lip pays.
aimCentre.4: Coins that slide off the sides are simply gone. Fortunes fall off the front.

upgradeAffordable.0: You can now afford {{upgrade}}. Upgrades are just below.
upgradeAffordable.1: {{upgrade}} is within reach. A small indulgence, a lasting difference.
upgradeAffordable.2: If I may suggest {{upgrade}}: your purse can bear it.
upgradeAffordable.3: {{upgrade}} awaits you in Upgrades. I would not keep it waiting.
upgradeAffordable.4: {{upgrade}} is affordable. The table would thank you for it.

feedTower.0: Feed the Champagne Tower: coins that stack on it raise its payout.
feedTower.1: That tower is looking rather bare. Land a few coins on it.
feedTower.2: Coins stacked on the Champagne Tower bring it down in a jackpot cascade.
feedTower.3: The tower likes company. Feed it, and it will return the favour.
feedTower.4: Do not neglect the Champagne Tower. A tall one falls gloriously.

idle.0: Your coins are getting restless. Tap the table to drop one.
idle.1: The pusher waits for no one. A coin, perhaps? Just tap the table.
idle.2: Woolgathering? Tap anywhere on the table to drop a coin.
idle.3: A quiet moment. The table would welcome another coin.
idle.4: Coins in hand earn nothing, I am afraid. Tap to drop one in.

arrived.0: Another crate has arrived. Push it home.
arrived.1: A delivery for you. Nudge that crate over the edge.
arrived.2: Ah, a Vault Crate. Somebody has been thinking of you.
arrived.3: A crate on the table. I wonder what is inside. Well, you will.
arrived.4: Fresh cargo. Do see it safely over the edge.

modest.0: {{rarity}}. Modest, but every collection starts somewhere.
modest.1: {{rarity}}. Charming, in its own quiet way.
modest.2: {{rarity}}. Not every evening can be a gala.
modest.3: Ah. {{rarity}}. I shall find it a nice shelf.
modest.4: Modest. Still, one never sniffs at a gift.

rare.1: Oh, {{rarity}}. That will look splendid in the lounge.
rare.2: {{rarity}}. I do enjoy watching your luck improve.
rare.4: {{rarity}}. The other guests will want to know your secret.

legendary.1: {{rarity}}. I need a chair, and possibly a brandy.
legendary.2: {{rarity}}! Thirty years in this house and I have seldom seen one.
legendary.3: Good gracious. {{rarity}}. Hold it up to the light.
legendary.4: {{rarity}}! The house will talk of nothing else.

empty.0: The Vault is empty. Wait a moment; the Steward will slip you a few coins.
empty.1: Out of coins? The ones still sliding may yet fall. If not, the Steward obliges.
empty.2: An empty Vault happens to the best of us. The Steward is on his way.
empty.3: Nothing in hand. Watch the ledge; coins on the table still count once they fall.
empty.4: Do not despair. The Steward tops up an empty Vault after a short pause.

welcomeBack.0: Welcome back. The house kept pushing: {{coins}} coins collected.
welcomeBack.1: While you were away, the table earned {{coins}}. I took the liberty.
welcomeBack.2: Ah, you return. {{coins}} coins, kept warm for you.
welcomeBack.3: Welcome back. The night staff collected {{coins}} on your behalf.
welcomeBack.4: {{coins}} coins while you rested. The house never sleeps.

capped.0: Welcome back. The Vault filled up at {{coins}}; a larger one would hold more.
capped.1: {{coins}} collected, but the Vault was full. More room means more waiting for you.
capped.2: The Vault overflowed at {{coins}}. An upgrade would widen it.
capped.3: Full to the brim: {{coins}}. The Vault could do with more room.
capped.4: {{coins}}, and not a coin more; the Vault was full. Upgrades can fix that.

purchased.1: {{upgrade}}, improved. The table already looks happier.
purchased.4: {{upgrade}} at level {{level}}. I shall inform the staff.

wobbling.0: The tower is wobbling! Steady… steady…
wobbling.1: Mind the tower! It is about to go.
wobbling.2: It sways! Somebody hold my monocle.
wobbling.3: Oh dear, oh dear. The tower is leaning.
wobbling.4: Any moment now. I cannot look. I am looking.

arrived.0: Welcome to {{venue}}. Your reputation precedes you.
arrived.1: {{venue}}. I took the liberty of arriving first.
arrived.2: A new address: {{venue}}. Do try to behave. Or do not.
arrived.3: Welcome to {{venue}}. Same Concierge, finer view.
arrived.4: {{venue}}, at last. Your luggage is already in the suite.
